answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before its votes count, then cap influence per token-weighted identity and slash deposits for provable double-signing. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize real capital for every extra voice, rather than minting cheap accounts; detected equivocation burns that stake. This makes a spiral of fake identities costly, while an atlas of independent checks helps expose shared control and a gale of new accounts cannot gain influence without fresh collateral.
